Pairs (angle 1, angle 2) and (angle 3, angle 4) are supplementary because they are adjacent angles on a straight line (Theorem 1). Angle 1 and angle 4, and angle 3 and angle 2, are alternate interior angles but are not equal because the two lines are not parallel — alternate interior angles are equal only when the lines are parallel (Theorem 7). Same-side interior angles are supplementary when the two lines cut by the transversal are parallel (Corollary 2 of Theorem 7). Two non-parallel lines meet when extended on the side where the same-side interior angles together are less than 180 degrees, forming a triangle with the transversal; by Theorem 6 the exterior angle of that triangle is greater than each remote interior angle.

Remember

  • SAS (Theorem 4) proves most results in this exercise: two sides and the included angle.
  • Vertical angles (Theorem 3) give the equal included angle in crossing-lines proofs.
  • All angles of a rectangle are 90 degrees.
  • In an isosceles triangle, the vertex-angle bisector is perpendicular to the base.
  • Every point on the perpendicular bisector of a segment is equidistant from its ends.
  • Medians of the equal sides of an isosceles triangle are equal.
  • Only one perpendicular can be drawn from an exterior point to a line.
  • Alternate interior angles are equal only when the lines are parallel (Theorem 7).

mcqs.q: Which congruence rule is Theorem 4, used in most proofs of Exercise 10.4?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is SAS. Theorem 4 is the side-angle-side rule: two sides and the included angle prove the triangles congruent.

mcqs.q: In Q1, why is angle AOC congruent to angle BOD?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is They are vertical angles, Theorem 3. The two lines cut at O, so opposite angles AOC and BOD are vertical and equal.

mcqs.q: In Q1, after triangle AOC is congruent to triangle BOD, AC congruent to BD follows because they are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Corresponding sides of congruent triangles. Once SAS proves the triangles congruent, their corresponding sides AC and BD are congruent.

mcqs.q: Each angle of a rectangle measures:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 90 degrees. Starting from angle A = 90 degrees and using parallel sides, angles B, C and D are each also 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: In an isosceles triangle with AB congruent to AC, the bisector of angle A is ___ to BC.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Perpendicular. SAS gives angle ADB = angle ADC, and since they add to 180 degrees, each is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: Every point on the perpendicular bisector of AB is ___ from A and B.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Equidistant. The SAS proof with triangles AOP and BOP shows AP congruent to BP for any point P on the bisector.

mcqs.q: The medians of the equal sides of an isosceles triangle are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Equal to each other. Triangles ABD and ACE are congruent by SAS, so BD congruent to CE, the two medians.

mcqs.q: Why can only one perpendicular be drawn from an exterior point to a line?
options: Two perpendiculars would make a triangle with two right angles, contradicting Corollary 1 of Theorem 6
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Two perpendiculars would make a triangle with two right angles, contradicting Corollary 1 of Theorem 6. A triangle has at most one right angle, so the supposition fails.

mcqs.q: Alternate interior angles are equal only when the two lines are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Parallel. Theorem 7 gives equality of alternate interior angles only for parallel lines, as stressed in Question 8.

mcqs.q: Same-side interior angles are supplementary when the lines cut by the transversal are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Parallel. Corollary 2 of Theorem 7 says same-side interior angles are supplementary exactly in the parallel case.

lessons.title: Exercise 10.5
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

This exercise combines parallel lines (Theorems 7 and 8), congruent triangles by SAS, Theorem 5 (base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal) and Theorem 9 (angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees).

For Question 1, the key construction in words is: draw a line through the bend parallel to the two parallel lines, then use alternate interior angles. Figure (a): the upper part is 180 degrees - 130 degrees = 50 degrees and the lower part is 40 degrees, so x = 50 degrees + 40 degrees = 90 degrees. Figure (b): the 135 degree bend splits into 75 degrees and 60 degrees; x is the supplement of 60 degrees, so x = 180 degrees - 60 degrees = 120 degrees. Figure (c): drawing a line through the dent parallel to the edges gives alternate interior angles 25 degrees and 30 degrees, so the dent angle x = 25 degrees + 30 degrees = 55 degrees. Figure (d): a triangle has angles 40 degrees (vertical angle of the given 40 degrees), 75 degrees and x, so by Theorem 9, x = 180 degrees - 40 degrees - 75 degrees = 65 degrees.

Proof — AC Parallel to BD and AD Parallel to BC

Statement: If two lines AB and CD cut each other at point O (with O the midpoint of both), prove that AC and BD are parallel and AD and BC are parallel.

Given: AB and CD cut each other at O, OA congruent to OB and OC congruent to OD.

To Prove: AC parallel to BD and AD parallel to BC.

Construction: Join A to C, B to D, A to D and B to C to form the triangles at the crossing.

Proof:

In triangle AOC and triangle BOD: OA congruent to OB, OC congruent to OD, angle AOC congruent to angle BOD (vertical).

Hence triangle AOC congruent to triangle BOD (SAS).

So angle OAC = angle OBD (alternate interior angles).

Hence AC parallel to BD (Theorem 8).

Similarly triangle AOD congruent to triangle BOC, so angle OAD = angle OBC.

Hence AD parallel to BC.

Q.E.D.

Proof — Midpoint Segment: CF Parallel to AB and DE Parallel to BC

Statement: D and E are the midpoints of sides AB and AC of triangle ABC. If DE is extended to point F so that EF congruent to DE, prove that CF parallel to AB and DE parallel to BC.

Given: D is the midpoint of AB, E is the midpoint of AC, and DE is extended to F with EF congruent to DE.

To Prove: CF parallel to AB and DE parallel to BC.

Construction: Extend DE beyond E to F so that EF congruent to DE, and join C to F.

Proof:

In triangle ADE and triangle CFE: AE congruent to CE (E is the midpoint of AC).

Angle AED congruent to angle CEF (vertical angles).

DE congruent to EF (given).

Hence triangle ADE congruent to triangle CFE (SAS).

Hence CF congruent to AD and angle A congruent to angle ECF.

Angle A and angle ECF are alternate interior angles, so CF parallel to AB (Theorem 8).

Moreover, CF congruent to AD congruent to BD (D is the midpoint of AB), so DBCF is a parallelogram (one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel).

So DF parallel to BC, that is, DE parallel to BC.

Q.E.D.

Proof — Opposite Angles of a Parallelogram Are Equal

Statement: The opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal to each other.

Given: ABCD is a parallelogram (AB parallel to CD, AD parallel to BC).

To Prove: Angle A = angle C and angle B = angle D.

Construction: No extra construction is needed; use the sides as transversals.

Proof:

AB is a transversal cutting AD and BC, so m angle A + m angle B = 180 degrees (same-side interior angles, Corollary 2 of Theorem 8).

Similarly BC is a transversal cutting AB and CD, so m angle B + m angle C = 180 degrees.

Hence m angle A + m angle B = m angle B + m angle C, so m angle A = m angle C.

Similarly m angle B = m angle D.

Hence the opposite angles are equal.

Q.E.D.

Question 5: In an isosceles triangle the two base angles are equal (Theorem 5) and each is less than 90 degrees, because the angles sum to 180 degrees (Theorem 9); if one base angle were 90 degrees or more, the sum would exceed 180 degrees. The vertex angle = 180 degrees - 2 times (base angle), so the vertex angle can be acute, right (90 degrees, with each base angle 45 degrees), or obtuse (less than 180 degrees).

Question 6: One angle of a triangle equals the sum of the other two exactly when the triangle is right-angled. If A = B + C and A + B + C = 180 degrees (Theorem 9), then A + A = 180 degrees, so A = 90 degrees, and the other two sum to 90 degrees (Corollary 3 of Theorem 9).

Proof — Sum of Interior Angles of a Quadrilateral

Statement: The sum of the interior angles of any quadrilateral is the sum of four right angles.

Given: Any quadrilateral.

To Prove: The interior angles sum to 4 right angles = 360 degrees.

Construction: Draw any one diagonal of the quadrilateral.

Proof:

The diagonal divides the quadrilateral into two triangles.

Each triangle's angles sum to 180 degrees = 2 right angles (Theorem 9).

Hence the sum of the quadrilateral's interior angles = 2 right angles + 2 right angles = 4 right angles = 360 degrees.

Q.E.D.

Remember

  • To find a bend angle between parallel lines, draw a line through the bend parallel to them and add alternate interior angles.
  • Equal alternate interior angles prove lines parallel by Theorem 8.
  • Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal.
  • Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal (Theorem 5) and each is less than 90 degrees.
  • If one angle of a triangle equals the sum of the other two, that angle is 90 degrees.
  • Angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees (Theorem 9); angles of a quadrilateral sum to 360 degrees.

mcqs.q: In Q1 figure (a), x = 50 degrees + 40 degrees equals:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 90 degrees. Drawing a line through the bend parallel to the parallel lines gives parts 50 degrees and 40 degrees, which add to 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: In Q1 figure (b), x is the supplement of 60 degrees, so x equals:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 120 degrees. Supplementary angles add to 180 degrees, so x = 180 degrees minus 60 degrees equals 120 degrees.

mcqs.q: In Q1 figure (c), the dent angle x = 25 degrees + 30 degrees equals:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 55 degrees. The line through the dent parallel to the edges gives alternate interior angles 25 degrees and 30 degrees that add to 55 degrees.

mcqs.q: In Q1 figure (d), x = 180 - 40 - 75 degrees equals:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 65 degrees. By Theorem 9 the angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees, so x = 180 minus 40 minus 75 equals 65 degrees.

mcqs.q: Equal alternate interior angles are used to prove lines parallel by which theorem?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Theorem 8. In Q2 and Q3, equal alternate interior angles give AC parallel to BD and CF parallel to AB by Theorem 8.

mcqs.q: The opposite angles of a parallelogram are:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Equal to each other. Using same-side interior sums of 180 degrees for both pairs gives angle A = angle C and angle B = angle D.

mcqs.q: Each base angle of an isosceles triangle must be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Less than 90 degrees. The base angles are equal by Theorem 5 and the total is 180 degrees by Theorem 9, so each base angle is below 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: If the vertex angle of an isosceles triangle is 90 degrees, each base angle is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 45 degrees. The two equal base angles share 180 minus 90 equals 90 degrees, so each is 45 degrees.

mcqs.q: One angle of a triangle equals the sum of the other two. That angle must be:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 90 degrees. If A = B + C and A + B + C = 180 degrees, then 2A = 180 degrees, so A = 90 degrees and the triangle is right-angled.

mcqs.q: The sum of the interior angles of any quadrilateral is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 360 degrees. A diagonal splits the quadrilateral into two triangles, each summing to 180 degrees, giving 4 right angles in total.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 10
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

Demonstrative geometry is a branch of mathematics. Its important work is to prove geometrical statements (propositions) by logical reasoning and proof — to establish facts about figures by reasoning, not merely by looking or measuring.

Undefined terms are the basic terms which are not defined, but are understood directly, such as point, line and plane. All of geometry rests on them.

Assumptions are statements accepted without proof, on which proofs rest. They are of two kinds: axioms and postulates. A postulate is the fundamental assumption which concerns geometry and is accepted without proof, such as 'exactly one line can be drawn through two different points'. An axiom is the fundamental assumption which applies generally to all of mathematics and is accepted without proof, such as 'if a = b and b = c, then a = c' (the transitive property of equality).

Propositions are statements that are to be proved or that are proved, such as a theorem, a corollary and a rider/problem. Every proposition is proved by reasoning. A corollary is a proposition which follows directly from another proposition and needs little separate proof, such as the corollaries of Theorem 1.

The four important elements of deductive reasoning are: (1) defined terms, (2) undefined terms, (3) propositions, (4) assumptions. In the working form of a proof there are also four parts: given, required to prove, construction, proof.

Fill-in facts from Question 8(b): On a plane, infinitely many lines are determined from every point. In a plane, exactly one line is determined by two different points. From a point not on a line, more than one perpendicular cannot be drawn. If two lines are parallel to each other, their alternate angles and corresponding angles are equal to each other. The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its remote interior angles.

True statements from Question 8(a), in their correct form: If two lines cut each other, their vertical angles are equal (Theorem 3) — true. From any point outside a line, only one line parallel to that line can be drawn — true. The sum of the three angles of a triangle is 180 degrees (Theorem 9) — true. If a ray emerges from a point on a line, the two angles formed cannot be complementary, because they are supplementary (Theorem 1) — so that complementary claim is false. An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its remote interior angles (Corollary 5 of Theorem 9) — true.

Proof — Theorem 1

Statement: Theorem 1: The sum of the angles formed at any point on a straight line is 180 degrees (2 right angles).

Given: AB is a straight line and O is a point on it, from which ray OP emerges.

To Prove: The angles at O on the line sum to 180 degrees.

Construction: Draw OP perpendicular to AB.

Proof:

m angle AOP + m angle POB = 180 degrees, because together they make the straight line AB.

Hence the sum of the angles formed at a point on a straight line is 180 degrees.

Q.E.D.

Proof — Angles on the Same Side of a Line Sum to 2 Right Angles

Statement: The sum of the angles formed on the same side of any line is 2 right angles.

Given: AB is a line and O is a point on it, and several rays on the same side form angles angle 1, angle 2, angle 3, and so on.

To Prove: Angle 1 + angle 2 + angle 3 + ... = 180 degrees = 2 right angles.

Construction: No extra construction is needed.

Proof:

By Theorem 1, the whole angle between the first and last rays is 180 degrees.

That whole angle is the sum of all these small angles.

Hence angle 1 + angle 2 + angle 3 + ... = 180 degrees = 2 right angles.

Q.E.D.

Proof — Vertical Angles Are Equal (Theorem 3)

Statement: If two lines cut each other, their vertical angles are equal to each other.

Given: Two lines cut each other, forming four angles.

To Prove: The vertical angles are equal.

Construction: No extra construction is needed.

Proof:

Any two adjacent angles sum to 180 degrees (Theorem 1).

Hence angle 1 + angle 2 = 180 degrees and angle 3 + angle 2 = 180 degrees, so angle 1 = angle 3.

Similarly angle 2 = angle 4.

Hence the vertical angles are equal (Theorem 3).

Q.E.D.

Proof — Theorem 5: Base Angles of an Isosceles Triangle Are Equal

Statement: Theorem 5: The base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal to each other.

Given: Triangle ABC has AB congruent to AC.

To Prove: Angle B = angle C.

Construction: Draw the bisector AD of angle A, meeting BC at D.

Proof:

In triangle ABD and triangle ACD: AB congruent to AC.

Angle BAD congruent to angle CAD (AD is the bisector).

AD is common.

Hence triangle ABD congruent to triangle ACD (SAS, Theorem 4).

Hence angle B = angle C, that is, the base angles are equal (Theorem 5).

Q.E.D.

Proof — From a Point, Only One Perpendicular Can Be Drawn to a Line

Statement: From a point, only one perpendicular can be drawn to a line.

Given: An exterior point P and a line l.

To Prove: Only one perpendicular can be drawn from P to l (Corollary 2 of Theorem 6).

Construction: Suppose, for contradiction, two perpendiculars PA and PB are drawn from P to line l.

Proof:

Suppose the contrary: from an exterior point P, two perpendiculars PA and PB can be drawn to line l.

Then triangle PAB would have two right angles, which contradicts Corollary 1 of Theorem 6 (a triangle has at most one right angle).

Hence the supposition is false, and only one perpendicular can be drawn from P to l.

Q.E.D.

Proof — Exterior Angle Equals Sum of Remote Interior Angles

Statement: The exterior angle of any triangle equals the sum of the remote interior angles.

Given: Triangle ABC has BC extended to D, so angle ACD is the exterior angle.

To Prove: Angle ACD = angle A + angle B.

Construction: Extend BC to D.

Proof:

The angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees (Theorem 9): angle A + angle B + angle ACB = 180 degrees.

And angle ACD + angle ACB = 180 degrees (angles on a straight line).

Hence angle ACD + angle ACB = angle A + angle B + angle ACB.

So angle ACD = angle A + angle B.

Q.E.D.

Question 9 in words: the figure contains parallel pairs AB parallel to CD, AB parallel to FG, FG parallel to CD and EF parallel to GC. Using alternate interior angles (Theorem 7) with different transversals gives a = b, b = c and c = d, so m angle a = m angle b = m angle c = m angle d. Angle-chasing examples: 42 degrees = 20 degrees + x, so x = 22 degrees; x as an exterior angle with remote interiors 75 degrees and 50 degrees gives x = 125 degrees (Corollary 5 of Theorem 9); and a 60 degree angle splitting into 40 degrees and x gives x = 20 degrees.

Remember

  • Demonstrative geometry proves propositions by logical reasoning, not by measuring.
  • Undefined terms include point, line and plane; assumptions are axioms and postulates.
  • A postulate concerns geometry; an axiom applies to all of mathematics.
  • A corollary follows directly from another proposition with little separate proof.
  • Theorem 1: angles at a point on a straight line sum to 180 degrees.
  • Theorem 3: vertical angles are equal. Theorem 5: base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal. Theorem 9: angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees.
  • An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of its remote interior angles.
  • From a point not on a line, only one perpendicular and only one parallel can be drawn.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.1
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

In a right triangle, the side opposite the right angle is the hypotenuse. It is the longest side.

For any acute angle, the side in front of the angle is the opposite side. The side next to the angle, apart from the hypotenuse, is the adjacent side.

The six trigonometric ratios are made from these three sides. Changing the angle changes which leg is opposite and which is adjacent.

Sin = Opposite / Hypotenuse

Cos = Adjacent / Hypotenuse

Tan = Opposite / Adjacent

Cot = Adjacent / Opposite

Sec = Hypotenuse / Adjacent

Cosec = Hypotenuse / Opposite

Sin × Cosec = 1

Cos × Sec = 1

Tan × Cot = 1

Tan = Sin / Cos

Cot = Cos / Sin

If the two acute angles are x and y, then x + y = 90 degrees. They are complementary angles.

Sin x = Cos y

Cos x = Sin y

Tan x = Cot y

Cot x = Tan y

Sec x = Cosec y

Cosec x = Sec y

Note on Question 4 of this exercise: the measures printed in its figure, 16, 24 and 30, do not satisfy the Pythagoras theorem. The book therefore proves the results with general sides a, b and c. The identities themselves are correct because they follow from x + y = 90 degrees alone.

Worked Example

Example: In right triangle PQR, PQ = 15 cm, PR = 12 cm and QR = 9 cm. Find the six ratios for angle P.

Step 1: For angle P, the opposite side is QR = 9 cm.

Step 2: For angle P, the adjacent side is PR = 12 cm.

Step 3: The hypotenuse is PQ = 15 cm.

Step 4: Sin P = Opposite / Hypotenuse = 9 / 15 = 3/5.

Step 5: Cos P = Adjacent / Hypotenuse = 12 / 15 = 4/5.

Step 6: Tan P = Opposite / Adjacent = 9 / 12 = 3/4.

Step 7: Cot P = Adjacent / Opposite = 12 / 9 = 4/3.

Step 8: Sec P = Hypotenuse / Adjacent = 15 / 12 = 5/4.

Step 9: Cosec P = Hypotenuse / Opposite = 15 / 9 = 5/3.

Remember

  • First name the opposite side, adjacent side and hypotenuse for the chosen angle.
  • Sin and Cosec are reciprocals. Cos and Sec are reciprocals. Tan and Cot are reciprocals.
  • Tan = Sin / Cos and Cot = Cos / Sin.
  • In triangle LMN of the exercise, Sin x = Cos y = 4/5, Tan x = Cot y = 4/3 and Cos x = Sin y = 3/5.
  • For complementary angles, a ratio of one angle equals the matching ratio of the other angle.

mcqs.q: In right triangle PQR, PQ = 15 cm, PR = 12 cm, QR = 9 cm. What is Sin P?
mcqs.why: Sin P = opposite / hypotenuse = QR / PQ = 9/15 = 3/5. The correct answer is 3/5, using opposite over hypotenuse for angle P.

mcqs.q: In the same triangle PQR, what is Cos P?
mcqs.why: Cos P = adjacent / hypotenuse = PR / PQ = 12/15 = 4/5. The correct answer is 4/5, using adjacent over hypotenuse.

mcqs.q: In the same triangle PQR, what is Tan P?
mcqs.why: Tan P = opposite / adjacent = QR / PR = 9/12 = 3/4. The correct answer is 3/4, not its reciprocal 4/3.

mcqs.q: In the same triangle PQR, what is Cosec P?
mcqs.why: Cosec P = hypotenuse / opposite = PQ / QR = 15/9 = 5/3. The correct answer is 5/3, the reciprocal of Sin P.

mcqs.q: In triangle PQR, for angle Q the opposite side is PR = 12 cm and the hypotenuse is PQ = 15 cm. What is Sin Q?
mcqs.why: Sin Q = opposite / hypotenuse = 12/15 = 4/5. The correct answer is 4/5. For angle Q, PR becomes the opposite side.

mcqs.q: In triangle PQR, what is Cot Q?
mcqs.why: Cot Q = adjacent / opposite = QR / PR = 9/12 = 3/4. The correct answer is 3/4, which also equals Tan P.

mcqs.q: In triangle PQR, what is Sec Q?
mcqs.why: Sec Q = hypotenuse / adjacent = PQ / QR = 15/9 = 5/3. The correct answer is 5/3, the reciprocal of Cos Q.

mcqs.q: In triangle LMN, l = 20 cm, m = 16 cm, n = 12 cm, and x is angle M. What is Sin x?
mcqs.why: Sin x = opposite / hypotenuse = m / l = 16/20 = 4/5. The correct answer is 4/5, after simplifying 16/20.

mcqs.q: In triangle LMN, what is Cos x?
mcqs.why: Cos x = adjacent / hypotenuse = n / l = 12/20 = 3/5. The correct answer is 3/5, using the side next to x.

mcqs.q: In triangle LMN, what is Tan y, where y is angle N?
mcqs.why: Tan y = opposite / adjacent = n / m = 12/16 = 3/4. The correct answer is 3/4, which equals Cot x.

mcqs.q: Which pair is equal in triangle LMN?
mcqs.why: Sin x = 4/5 and Cos y = 4/5, so Sin x = Cos y. The correct answer is Sin x = Cos y, a complementary-angle pair.

mcqs.q: In triangle UVW, Sin alpha = 15/17 and Cosec alpha = 17/15. What is Sin alpha x Cosec alpha?
mcqs.why: Sin alpha x Cosec alpha = (15/17) x (17/15) = 1. The correct answer is 1 because Sin and Cosec are reciprocals.

mcqs.q: For angle beta in triangle UVW, Sin beta = 8/17 and Cos beta = 15/17. What is Sin beta / Cos beta?
mcqs.why: Sin beta / Cos beta = (8/17) / (15/17) = 8/15, which is Tan beta. The correct answer is 8/15.

mcqs.q: For angle alpha, Cos alpha = 8/17 and Sin alpha = 15/17. What is Cos alpha / Sin alpha?
mcqs.why: Cos alpha / Sin alpha = (8/17) / (15/17) = 8/15, which is Cot alpha. The correct answer is 8/15.

mcqs.q: In a right triangle the acute angles are x and y, so x + y = 90 degrees. Which statement is true?
mcqs.why: Sec x = hypotenuse / adjacent to x and Cosec y = hypotenuse / opposite to y give the same side ratio, c/b. The correct answer is Sec x = Cosec y.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.2
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

Some angles occur again and again: 30 degrees, 45 degrees and 60 degrees. Their ratios have exact values. Learn the table and use it without a calculator.

To find an unknown acute angle, match its ratio with the same ratio in the table. For example, if Cos x = 1/2, compare it with the table and take x = 60 degrees.

AngleSinCosTanCotSecCosec
30°1/2√3/21/√3√32/√32
45°1/√21/√211√2√2
60°√3/21/2√31/√322/√3

Sin 30° = 1/2

Cos 30° = √3/2

Sin 45° = Cos 45° = 1/√2

Tan 45° = 1

Complementary angles also give a quick rule. A ratio at an angle equals the matching ratio at 90 degrees minus that angle.

Sin θ = Cos (90° − θ)

Tan θ = Cot (90° − θ)

Sec θ = Cosec (90° − θ)

Worked Example

Example: Find Sin 30° x Sin 60° + Cos 30° x Cos 60°.

Step 1: Write the table values. Sin 30° = 1/2.

Step 2: Sin 60° = √3/2.

Step 3: Cos 30° = √3/2.

Step 4: Cos 60° = 1/2.

Step 5: Substitute: (1/2)(√3/2) + (√3/2)(1/2).

Step 6: Multiply each pair: √3/4 + √3/4.

Step 7: Add: 2√3/4 = √3/2.

Remember

  • Learn the full 30, 45 and 60 degree table, including Cot, Sec and Cosec as reciprocals.
  • To find an angle, first name the ratio, then match its exact value in the table.
  • Expressions can give 0 or a negative value, for example Tan 30° x Cot 60° − Sin 45° x Cos 45° = −1/6.
  • Use 90° − angle for Sin-Cos, Tan-Cot and Sec-Cosec pairs.
  • Examples: Sin 35° = Cos 55°, Tan 65° = Cot 25° and Cosec 75° = Sec 15°.

mcqs.q: If Cos x = √3/2, what is x?
mcqs.why: From the table Cos 30 degrees = root3/2, so Cos x = Cos 30 degrees gives x = 30 degrees. The correct answer is 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: If Tan y = √3, what is y?
mcqs.why: From the table Tan 60 degrees = root3, so Tan y = Tan 60 degrees gives y = 60 degrees. The correct answer is 60 degrees.

mcqs.q: If Cosec A = 2, what is angle A?
mcqs.why: From the table Cosec 30 degrees = 2, so angle A = 30 degrees. The correct answer is 30 degrees, the reciprocal pair of Sin 30 = 1/2.

mcqs.q: What is Sin 30° x Sin 60° + Cos 30° x Cos 60°?
mcqs.why: Substitute 1/2, root3/2, root3/2 and 1/2: the sum is root3/4 + root3/4 = root3/2. The correct answer is root3/2.

mcqs.q: What is Sec 30° x Cosec 60° + Tan 60° x Cot 30°?
mcqs.why: Sec 30 x Cosec 60 = (2/root3)(2/root3) = 4/3 and Tan 60 x Cot 30 = root3 x root3 = 3, total 13/3. The correct answer is 13/3.

mcqs.q: What is Sin 60° x Sin 45° − Cos 30° x Cos 45°?
mcqs.why: Both products are (root3/2)(1/root2), so subtracting equal products gives 0. The correct answer is 0.

mcqs.q: If Sin 30° = Cos x, what is x?
mcqs.why: Sin 30 degrees = 1/2 and Cos 60 degrees = 1/2, so x = 60 degrees. The correct answer is 60 degrees, the complement of 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: If Tan 60° = Cot x, what is x?
mcqs.why: Tan 60 degrees = root3 and Cot 30 degrees = root3, so x = 30 degrees. The correct answer is 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: Sin 35° = Cos ___ . Fill the blank.
mcqs.why: Use the complementary rule: 90 degrees minus 35 degrees = 55 degrees, so Sin 35 = Cos 55. The correct answer is 55 degrees.

mcqs.q: Cos 56° = Sin ___ . Fill the blank.
mcqs.why: Use the complementary rule: 90 degrees minus 56 degrees = 34 degrees, so Cos 56 = Sin 34. The correct answer is 34 degrees.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.3
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

To solve a right triangle means to find all its unknown sides and unknown angles.

First use the angle sum: the right angle is 90 degrees, so the other two angles add to 90 degrees.

Second acute angle = 90° − given acute angle

Then choose a ratio that contains the known side and the side you want.

Sin = Opposite / Hypotenuse

Cos = Adjacent / Hypotenuse

Tan = Opposite / Adjacent

When two sides are known, find an angle from a ratio value in the standard table, or find the third side with Pythagoras.

Hypotenuse² = Leg² + Leg²

AngleSinCosTan
30°1/2√3/21/√3
45°1/√21/√21
60°√3/21/2√3

Worked Example

Example: Solve triangle ABC with angle C = 90°, angle A = 30° and BC = 3 cm.

Step 1: Find angle B.

Step 2: Angle B = 90° − angle A.

Step 3: Angle B = 90° − 30° = 60°.

Step 4: Use Sin A for BC and hypotenuse AB.

Step 5: Sin 30° = BC / AB.

Step 6: 1/2 = 3 / AB.

Step 7: Cross-multiply: AB = 6 cm.

Step 8: Use Tan A for BC and AC.

Step 9: Tan 30° = BC / AC.

Step 10: 1/√3 = 3 / AC.

Step 11: AC = 3√3 cm.

Remember

  • Always find the second acute angle first with 90° minus the given angle.
  • Pick Sin, Cos or Tan according to the sides you know and the side you need.
  • If two legs are known, Tan gives an angle: for example Tan L = 1/√3 gives L = 30°.
  • If a leg and hypotenuse are known, Sin gives an angle: for example Sin A = 1/2 gives A = 30°.
  • Use Pythagoras for the remaining side when a ratio is not the shortest route.
  • At 45° the two legs are equal, so the hypotenuse is leg x √2.

mcqs.q: Triangle ABC has angle C = 90°, angle A = 30°, BC = 3 cm. What is angle B?
mcqs.why: Angle B = 90 degrees minus angle A = 90 minus 30 = 60 degrees. The correct answer is 60 degrees.

mcqs.q: In the same triangle ABC, what is hypotenuse AB?
mcqs.why: Sin 30 = BC/AB gives 1/2 = 3/AB, so AB = 6 cm. The correct answer is 6 cm.

mcqs.q: In the same triangle ABC, what is AC?
mcqs.why: Tan 30 = BC/AC gives 1/root3 = 3/AC, so AC = 3 root3 cm. The correct answer is 3 root3 cm.

mcqs.q: Triangle DEF has angle E = 90°, angle D = 60°, DE = 4 cm. What is DF?
mcqs.why: Cos 60 = DE/DF gives 1/2 = 4/DF, so DF = 8 cm. The correct answer is 8 cm, the hypotenuse.

mcqs.q: In the same triangle DEF, what is EF?
mcqs.why: Tan 60 = EF/DE gives root3 = EF/4, so EF = 4 root3 cm. The correct answer is 4 root3 cm.

mcqs.q: Triangle LMN has angle M = 90°, angle N = 45°, ML = 8 cm. What is MN?
mcqs.why: Tan 45 = ML/MN gives 1 = 8/MN, so MN = 8 cm. The correct answer is 8 cm; at 45 degrees the legs are equal.

mcqs.q: In the same triangle LMN, what is hypotenuse LN?
mcqs.why: LN = root of 8 squared plus 8 squared = root128 = 8 root2 cm. The correct answer is 8 root2 cm.

mcqs.q: Triangle LMN has l = 4 cm and n = 4√3 cm. Tan L = l/n = 1/√3. What is angle L?
mcqs.why: Tan 30 degrees = 1/root3, so angle L = 30 degrees. The correct answer is 30 degrees from the standard table.

mcqs.q: Triangle PQR has p = 6√3 cm and r = 6 cm, so Tan P = √3 and hypotenuse q = 12 cm. What is angle P?
mcqs.why: Tan 60 degrees = root3, so angle P = 60 degrees. The correct answer is 60 degrees; the other angle is then 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: Triangle ACB has a = 5 cm and c = 10 cm, so Sin A = 1/2. What is side b?
mcqs.why: Sin A = 1/2 gives A = 30 degrees, and b = root of 100 minus 25 = root75 = 5 root3 cm. The correct answer is 5 root3 cm.

lessons.title: Exercise 11.4
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

Many real problems form a right triangle: a ladder against a wall, a hill seen from the ground, a lighthouse and a ship, a flag pole, or a truck on a slope.

The angle between the ground and the line looking up to a top is the angle of elevation. The angle between the horizontal and the line looking down is the angle of elevation's partner, the angle of depression. The angle of depression from the top equals the angle of elevation from below, because they are alternate angles.

Draw the right triangle first. Mark the known side, the wanted side and the angle. Then pick the ratio that uses those two sides.

Cos = Adjacent / Hypotenuse

Tan = Opposite / Adjacent

Sin = Opposite / Hypotenuse

AngleSinCosTan
30°1/2√3/21/√3
45°1/√21/√21
60°√3/21/2√3

Note on Question 4 of this exercise: the book answer key lists 11.55 m, but that does not match the printed figure with base 173 m. 11.55 m would come from a 20 m base. With base 173 m the working below gives about 100 m, and that is the value used here.

Worked Example

Example: A ladder makes 60° with the floor. Its lower end is 3 m from the wall. Find the length of the ladder.

Step 1: Draw the right triangle. The wall and floor meet at 90°.

Step 2: The distance from the wall, 3 m, is the adjacent side to the 60° angle.

Step 3: The ladder itself is the hypotenuse. Call it L.

Step 4: The ratio with adjacent and hypotenuse is Cos.

Step 5: Cos 60° = Adjacent / Hypotenuse.

Step 6: Cos 60° = 3 / L.

Step 7: From the table, Cos 60° = 1/2.

Step 8: So 1/2 = 3 / L.

Step 9: Cross-multiply: L = 6 m.

Remember

  • Ladder problem: Cos 60° with foot 3 m from the wall gives ladder length 6 m.
  • Hill problem: Tan 45° = 1, so height equals distance; 200 m distance gives 200 m height.
  • Lighthouse problem: depression 30° becomes elevation 30°; Tan 30° gives distance = 170√3 m, about 294 m.
  • Flag problem: Tan 30° = height / 173, so height = 173/√3, about 100 m. The printed key value 11.55 m does not fit the figure.
  • Slope problem: Sin 30° = vertical climb / slope length; for 100 m slope the vertical climb is 50 m.

mcqs.q: A ladder makes 60° with the floor and its foot is 3 m from the wall. What is the length of the ladder?
mcqs.why: Cos 60 = 3 / length, and Cos 60 = 1/2, so length = 6 m. The correct answer is 6 m.

mcqs.q: Which ratio is used in the ladder problem, where the known side is adjacent and the wanted side is the hypotenuse?
mcqs.why: Adjacent over hypotenuse is Cos, so Cos 60 degrees is used for the ladder. The correct answer is Cos.

mcqs.q: The base of a hill is 200 m away and the angle of elevation is 45°. What is the height of the hill?
mcqs.why: Tan 45 = height/200 and Tan 45 = 1, so height = 200 m. The correct answer is 200 m.

mcqs.q: Which ratio is used for the hill problem, where height is opposite and distance is adjacent?
mcqs.why: Opposite over adjacent is Tan, so Tan 45 degrees links height and distance. The correct answer is Tan.

mcqs.q: A 170 m lighthouse is seen from a ship with angle of depression 30°. What is the distance of the ship from the base?
mcqs.why: Tan 30 = 170/distance gives 1/root3 = 170/distance, so distance = 170 root3 m, about 294 m. The correct answer is 170 root3 m.

mcqs.q: Why is the angle of elevation from the ship equal to the angle of depression from the lighthouse?
mcqs.why: The horizontal lines are parallel, so depression and elevation are alternate angles and are equal. The correct answer is alternate angles.

mcqs.q: For the flag with base 173 m and angle 30°, which equation gives its height?
mcqs.why: Tan 30 = height/173 and Tan 30 = 1/root3, so height = 173/root3, about 100 m. The correct answer is 173/root3.

mcqs.q: A truck climbs a 100 m slope at 30°. How much has it climbed vertically?
mcqs.why: Sin 30 = vertical/100 and Sin 30 = 1/2, so vertical climb = 50 m. The correct answer is 50 m.

mcqs.q: Which ratio is used in the truck slope problem, where vertical climb is opposite and slope length is the hypotenuse?
mcqs.why: Opposite over hypotenuse is Sin, so Sin 30 degrees links vertical climb and slope length. The correct answer is Sin.

mcqs.q: What is Tan 45°, used in the hill problem?
mcqs.why: From the standard table Tan 45 degrees = 1, which is why height equals distance in that problem. The correct answer is 1.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 11
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

The Review Exercise mixes all the work of this unit: standard-angle values, reciprocal and complementary identities, verification sums, and height-and-distance problems.

For a verification, work out the left-hand side step by step with table values and show it equals the right-hand side.

Sin 45° = Cos 45° = 1/√2

Cosec 45° = Sec 45° = √2

Cosec θ = 1 / Sin θ

Cot θ = 1 / Tan θ

Sec θ = 1 / Cos θ

Tan = 1 / Cot

Cos (90° − θ) = Sin θ

AngleSinCosTanCosecSecCot
30°1/2√3/21/√322/√3√3
45°1/√21/√21√2√21
60°√3/21/2√32/√321/√3

Worked Example

Example: A kite string makes 30° with the ground and the kite is 60 m above the ground. Find the length of the string.

Step 1: Draw the right triangle. The height, 60 m, is opposite the 30° angle.

Step 2: The string is the hypotenuse. Call it L.

Step 3: The ratio with opposite and hypotenuse is Sin.

Step 4: Sin 30° = Opposite / Hypotenuse.

Step 5: Sin 30° = 60 / L.

Step 6: From the table, Sin 30° = 1/2.

Step 7: So 1/2 = 60 / L.

Step 8: Cross-multiply: L = 120 m.

Remember

  • Verification sums: Cos 60° x Cos 30° − Sin 60° x Sin 30° = 0 and Sin 60° Cos 30° − Cos 60° Sin 30° = 1/2.
  • Also Sin 45° x Cos 45° + Sin 30° x Cos 60° = 3/4.
  • Canal problem: Tan 45° = 1, so a 9 m banner gives a canal width of 9 m.
  • Kite problem: Sin 30° = 1/2, so a height of 60 m gives a string of 120 m.
  • Reciprocals: Cosec 30° = 2, Cot 60° = 1/√3, Sec 30° = 2/√3.
  • Complementary pairs: Tan 30° = Cot 60° and Cosec 10° = Sec 80°.
  • False statements to watch: Cos is not 1/Sin, and Cosec is not 1/Sec; check every reciprocal carefully.

mcqs.q: What is Cos 60° x Cos 30° − Sin 60° x Sin 30°?
mcqs.why: The value is (1/2)(root3/2) minus (root3/2)(1/2) = root3/4 minus root3/4 = 0. The correct answer is 0.

mcqs.q: What is Sin 60° Cos 30° − Cos 60° Sin 30°?
mcqs.why: The value is (root3/2)(root3/2) minus (1/2)(1/2) = 3/4 minus 1/4 = 1/2. The correct answer is 1/2.

mcqs.q: What is Sin 45° x Cos 45° + Sin 30° x Cos 60°?
mcqs.why: The value is (1/root2)(1/root2) plus (1/2)(1/2) = 1/2 plus 1/4 = 3/4. The correct answer is 3/4.

mcqs.q: A 9 m banner across a canal is seen at 45° from the opposite bank. What is the width of the canal?
mcqs.why: Tan 45 = 9/width and Tan 45 = 1, so width = 9 m. The correct answer is 9 m.

mcqs.q: A kite is 60 m above the ground and its string makes 30° with the ground. What is the length of the string?
mcqs.why: Sin 30 = 60/length and Sin 30 = 1/2, so length = 120 m. The correct answer is 120 m.

mcqs.q: What is Cosec 30°?
mcqs.why: Cosec 30 = 1/Sin 30 = 1 divided by 1/2 = 2. The correct answer is 2, which also equals Sec 60 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is Cot 60°?
mcqs.why: Cot 60 = 1/Tan 60 = 1/root3, which also equals Tan 30 degrees. The correct answer is 1/root3.

mcqs.q: What is Cos 45°?
mcqs.why: From the standard table Cos 45 degrees = 1/root2, the same as Sin 45 degrees. The correct answer is 1/root2.

mcqs.q: What is Sec 30°?
mcqs.why: Sec 30 = 1/Cos 30 = 1 divided by root3/2 = 2/root3, the same as Cosec 60. The correct answer is 2/root3.

mcqs.q: What is Cos 60°?
mcqs.why: From the standard table Cos 60 degrees = 1/2. The correct answer is 1/2, not Sin 60 which is root3/2.

lessons.title: Review Exercise
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

Data are facts collected about something, for example marks obtained or time spent. A frequency tells how many times a value occurs. When we arrange values with their frequencies in a table, it is a frequency chart or frequency distribution.

For grouped data, each group is a class, for example 24-28. The two ends are the class limits. Because there is a gap between classes, we use true class limits by subtracting 0.5 from the lower limit and adding 0.5 to the upper limit.

The range shows the spread of the data.

Range = Largest value - Smallest value

True lower limit = Lower limit - 0.5

True upper limit = Upper limit + 0.5

Class width = Upper true limit - Lower true limit

Worked Example

Example: For classes 24-28, 29-33, 34-38, 39-43, 44-48 with frequencies 3, 16, 12, 23, 16, find class limits, true class limits and class width.

Step 1: Write each class as given.

ClassFrequencyClass limitsTrue class limitsUpper true limit
24-28324-2823.5-28.528.5
29-331629-3328.5-33.533.5
34-381234-3833.5-38.538.5
39-432339-4338.5-43.543.5
44-481644-4843.5-48.548.5

Step 2: For 24-28, true lower limit = 24 - 0.5 = 23.5.

Step 3: True upper limit = 28 + 0.5 = 28.5.

Step 4: Do the same for every class.

Step 5: Class width = 28.5 - 23.5 = 5.

Step 6: So the class width is 5 for every class.

Note: The book prints the third class as 38-34, which is wrong; the correct class is 34-38, used here. In Question 2, counting the printed marks gives 6 students with 4 marks and 3 students with 5 marks.

Remember

  • Frequency is how many times a value occurs.
  • True limits are found by -0.5 and +0.5.
  • Range = largest - smallest; for marks 0 to 6, range = 6.
  • The value with the highest frequency is obtained by the most people.
  • The value with the lowest frequency is obtained by the fewest people.
  • Total frequency must equal the total number of people.

mcqs.q: For the class 24-28, what are the true class limits?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 23.5-28.5. True lower limit = 24 - 0.5 = 23.5 and true upper limit = 28 + 0.5 = 28.5, which is the lesson point on true class limits.

mcqs.q: What is the class width for classes 24-28, 29-33, 34-38, 39-43, 44-48?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 5. Class width = 28.5 - 23.5 = 5. Every class in this table has the same width of 5.

mcqs.q: What is the upper true class limit of the class 39-43?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 43.5. Upper true limit = upper limit + 0.5 = 43 + 0.5 = 43.5 for the class 39-43.

mcqs.q: In the marks data (0 to 6), how many students obtained 3 marks?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 9. Counting the data, 3 marks occur 9 times, which is the highest frequency in that frequency chart.

mcqs.q: What is the range of the marks data 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 6. Range = largest value - smallest value = 6 - 0 = 6, using the range formula from this lesson.

mcqs.q: How many marks did the most students obtain in Question 2?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 3 marks. It has frequency 9, higher than any other mark, so the most students obtained 3 marks.

mcqs.q: How many marks did the fewest students obtain in Question 2?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 6 marks. Only 1 student obtained 6 marks, which is the lowest frequency in the chart.

mcqs.q: In the teachers survey, how many members took part in all?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 27 members. Total = 5 + 8 + 7 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 27, found by adding all frequencies.

mcqs.q: In the teachers survey, how many members spent the maximum time of 6 hours with children?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1 member. The frequency of 6 hours is 1, so only one member spent the maximum time.

mcqs.q: In the 150-person test, how many marks did the most people obtain?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 5 marks. Its frequency is 35, the highest frequency, so the most people (35) obtained 5 marks.

lessons.title: Exercise 12.1
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

In this exercise raw data are grouped into classes to make a frequency distribution. First we find the range, then we decide the class width, then we count how many values fall in each class.

A histogram is a bar graph for grouped data. True class limits are written on the X-axis and frequency is written on the Y-axis. The height of each bar is the frequency of that class. There is no gap between bars because true limits touch each other.

Range = Largest value - Smallest value

Class width = Range / Number of classes (rounded up)

True lower limit = Lower limit - 0.5

True upper limit = Upper limit + 0.5

Worked Example

Example: Weights of 30 boy scouts, smallest 29 kg and largest 47 kg. Make 5 classes.

Step 1: Range = 47 - 29 = 18.

Step 2: Class width = 18 / 5 = 3.6, rounded to 4.

Step 3: Make classes 29-32, 33-36, 37-40, 41-44, 45-48.

Step 4: Count the values in each class.

ClassTrue limitsFrequency
29-3228.5-32.54
33-3632.5-36.56
37-4036.5-40.58
41-4440.5-44.58
45-4844.5-48.54

Step 5: Check total: 4 + 6 + 8 + 8 + 4 = 30.

Step 6: For the histogram, write true limits on X-axis and frequency on Y-axis.

Step 7: Draw bars of heights 4, 6, 8, 8, 4 in order.

Remember

  • Always find range first, then class width.
  • Round class width up so all data are covered.
  • Use true limits for a histogram.
  • Bar height = frequency of the class.
  • Total of frequencies must equal total number of values.

mcqs.q: For the boy scouts weights, what is the range?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 18. Range = largest - smallest = 47 - 29 = 18, the first step in making classes.

mcqs.q: For the boy scouts weights with 5 classes, what class width is used?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 4. Class width = 18 / 5 = 3.6, rounded up to about 4 so the classes cover all weights.

mcqs.q: In the boy scouts distribution, what is the frequency of class 37-40?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8. Counting weights from 37 to 40 gives 8 scouts, as shown in the frequency table.

mcqs.q: For electricity use, range = 750 - 677. What is the range?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 73. Range = 750 - 677 = 73 units, before dividing by 5 classes to get the width.

mcqs.q: For electricity use with 5 classes, what is the frequency of class 692-706?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8. The table gives frequency 8 for 692-706, the highest bar in that histogram.

mcqs.q: In the monthly math test, what is the frequency of class 55-64?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 12. Twelve students scored 55-64, making it the tallest bar with true limits 54.5-64.5.

mcqs.q: For rainfall data, what is the range?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 23. Range = 26 - 3 = 23 cm, and 23 / 5 = 4.6 gives width about 5.

mcqs.q: In the rainfall distribution, what is the frequency of class 3-7?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8. Eight years had rainfall 3-7 cm, with true limits 2.5-7.5 in the table.

mcqs.q: For computer marks classes 26-30, 31-35 and so on, what are the true limits of 26-30?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 25.5-30.5. Subtract 0.5 from 26 and add 0.5 to 30 to get true limits for the histogram.

mcqs.q: In daily earnings, what is the frequency of class 1001-1100?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 35. Frequencies rise 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, so the last class 1001-1100 has frequency 35.

lessons.title: Exercise 12.2
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

The arithmetic mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency. They give a single value that represents the data.

The mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values. The median is the middle value when data are arranged in order. The mode is the value that occurs most often. Data may have one mode, two modes, or no mode.

In a weighted mean, each value has a weight. We multiply each value by its weight, add them, and divide by the sum of weights, not by the number of values.

Arithmetic mean X-bar = Sum of values / Number of values = Σx / n

Σx = n x X-bar

n = Σx / X-bar

Weighted mean = Σxw / Σw

Median (odd n) = middle value after arranging in order

Mode = value with highest frequency

Worked Example

Example: Find the weighted mean for values 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 with weights 1, 2, 1, 1, 2, 2, 1.

Step 1: Multiply each value by its weight: 10x1=10.

Step 2: 20x2=40.

Step 3: 30x1=30.

Step 4: 40x1=40.

Step 5: 50x2=100.

Step 6: 60x2=120.

Step 7: 70x1=70.

Step 8: Σxw = 10+40+30+40+100+120+70 = 410.

Step 9: Σw = 1+2+1+1+2+2+1 = 10.

Step 10: Weighted mean = 410 / 10 = 41.

Note: The book answer key writes 410/7, dividing by the count of values. That is wrong; we divide by the sum of weights, 10. The same correction applies to the other weighted-mean questions in this exercise, and for X-bar=13, n=11, Σx = 11x13 = 143, not 141 as printed in the key.

Remember

  • Mean = Σx / n; rearrange to find Σx or n when one is missing.
  • For weighted mean, divide by Σw, never by the count of values.
  • For median, always arrange data in order first.
  • For odd n, median is the single middle value.
  • Mode is the most frequent value; if no value repeats, there is no mode.
  • To find a missing value from the mean, use total = n x mean.

mcqs.q: Find the arithmetic mean of 3, 8, 5, 4, 6, 0, 7, 1, 2.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 4. Sum = 36 and n = 9, so mean = 36 / 9 = 4 using X-bar = Σx / n.

mcqs.q: Find the arithmetic mean of 11, 13, 15, 7, 9, 1, 3, 5.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 8. Sum = 64 and n = 8, so mean = 64 / 8 = 8 for this data set.

mcqs.q: Find the arithmetic mean of 11, 16, 13, 17, 10, 15, 18, 14, 12.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 14. Sum = 126 and n = 9, so mean = 126 / 9 = 14.

mcqs.q: Find the arithmetic mean of 1.2, 2.4, 3.6, 4.8, 5.1, 6.3, 7.5, 8.7.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 4.95. Sum = 39.6 and n = 8, so mean = 39.6 / 8 = 4.95.

mcqs.q: If X-bar = 12 and Σx = 132, what is n?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 11. n = Σx / X-bar = 132 / 12 = 11, rearranging the mean formula.

mcqs.q: If X-bar = 13 and n = 11, what is Σx?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 143. Σx = n x X-bar = 11 x 13 = 143. The printed key value 141 is a slip.

mcqs.q: Find the weighted mean of values 10-70 with Σxw = 410 and Σw = 10.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 41. Weighted mean = Σxw / Σw = 410 / 10 = 41, dividing by sum of weights, not by 7 values.

mcqs.q: Find the weighted mean when Σxw = 134 and Σw = 20.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 6.7. Weighted mean = 134 / 20 = 6.7, using the sum of weights as divisor.

mcqs.q: Find the weighted mean when Σxw = 50 and Σw = 10.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 5. Weighted mean = 50 / 10 = 5 for values 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 with their weights.
The correct answer is 11. In order 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 17, 19, the 5th (middle) value is 11.
The correct answer is 12. In order there are 11 values, so the 6th value is the median, which is 12.
The correct answer is 5.5. In order there are 13 values, the 7th value is 5.5, so the median is 5.5.

mcqs.q: Find the mode of 14, 21, 27, 14, 28, 29.
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 14. It occurs twice while all others occur once, so the mode is the most frequent value, 14.
The correct answer is 29. It occurs three times, more than 23 which occurs twice, so mode = 29.

mcqs.q: What is the mode of 93, 75, 85, 89, 77, 55, 33?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is No mode. No value occurs twice in this data, so there is no mode, an important case in this lesson.

lessons.title: Exercise 12.3
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

This exercise uses mean, median and mode together on real data, and uses the weighted mean when values have frequencies or weights, for example kilograms bought, or number of students at each mark.

For grouped frequency data, x is the value or mark and w or f is its frequency or weight. For even number of values, the median is the mean of the two middle values after arranging in order.

Weighted mean = Σxw / Σw

Arithmetic mean = Σx / n

Median (even n) = (middle value 1 + middle value 2) / 2

Mode = value with highest frequency

Worked Example

Example: Vegetables bought: potatoes 12 kg at Rs 25/kg, onions 8 kg at Rs 30, tomatoes 5 kg at Rs 60, carrots 3 kg at Rs 40, pinibon 4 kg at Rs 80. Find average price per kg.

Step 1: 12 x 25 = 300.

Step 2: 8 x 30 = 240.

Step 3: 5 x 60 = 300.

Step 4: 3 x 40 = 120.

Step 5: 4 x 80 = 320.

Step 6: Σxw = 300 + 240 + 300 + 120 + 320 = 1280.

Step 7: Σw = 12 + 8 + 5 + 3 + 4 = 32 kg.

Step 8: Average price = 1280 / 32 = 40 rupees per kg.

Note on heights question: the correct median is 138.5, not 138 as in the key, so Mode (140) >= Median (138.5) >= Mean (138.35) is correct. For rotten mangoes the correct mean is 37/20 = 1.85, not 1.75. For the test-marks question the printed Math frequencies add to 48, not 45.

Remember

  • Use weighted mean when each value has a weight or frequency.
  • For even n, median is the average of the two middle values.
  • Data can have two modes if two values share the highest frequency.
  • Compare averages to judge which group performed better.
  • Check totals: sum of frequencies must match the number given.

mcqs.q: What is the average price per kg of the vegetables in Question 1?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 40 rupees per kg. Σxw = 1280 and Σw = 32, so weighted mean = 1280 / 32 = 40.

mcqs.q: What is the arithmetic mean height of the 20 students?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 138.35 cm. Sum = 2767 and n = 20, so mean = 2767 / 20 = 138.35 cm.

mcqs.q: What is the median height of the 20 students?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 138.5 cm. Median = (10th + 11th) / 2 = (138 + 139) / 2 = 138.5 for even n = 20.

mcqs.q: What is the mode height of the 20 students?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 140 cm. It occurs three times, more than any other height, so mode = 140 cm.

mcqs.q: For the heights, is Mode >= Median >= Mean correct?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Yes, 140 >= 138.5 >= 138.35. With the correct median 138.5, the inequality holds for this data.

mcqs.q: What is the arithmetic mean number of rotten mangoes per crate?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 1.85. Sum = 37 and n = 20, so mean = 37 / 20 = 1.85 rotten mangoes per crate.

mcqs.q: What is the median number of rotten mangoes?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 2. Median = (10th + 11th) / 2 = (2 + 2) / 2 = 2 after arranging the 20 values in order.

mcqs.q: What are the modes for rotten mangoes?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 2 and 3. Each occurs five times, the highest frequency, so this data has two modes.

mcqs.q: In Question 4, which subject had the higher average marks?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Science, 48.22. Science average 2170/45 = 48.22 is higher than Math 2270/48 = 47.29, so students did better in Science.

mcqs.q: What is the average number per family in Question 5 (100 families, Σxw = 376)?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 3.76. Average = Σxw / total families = 376 / 100 = 3.76 per family.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 12
lessons.notes_html:
Concept

This review covers the whole unit: frequency distribution, histogram, and the three measures of central tendency - arithmetic mean, median and mode. Frequency distribution is the method of presenting raw data in a short and organized manner.

For a histogram, class midpoints can be used to estimate the mean of grouped data. The median class is the class where the middle value falls, found from cumulative frequencies. The modal class is the class with the highest frequency.

Arithmetic mean X-bar = Σx / n

Grouped mean = Σ(midpoint x frequency) / Total frequency

Median = middle value after arranging in order

Mode = value that occurs most often

Worked Example

Example: Marks out of 40 for 30 students, smallest 3 and largest 29. Make 5 classes.

Step 1: Range = 29 - 3 = 26.

Step 2: Class width = 26 / 5 = 5.2, rounded up to 6.

Step 3: Make classes 3-8, 9-14, 15-20, 21-26, 27-32.

Step 4: Count values in each class.

ClassTrue limitsFrequency
3-82.5-8.52
9-148.5-14.511
15-2014.5-20.56
21-2620.5-26.58
27-3226.5-32.53

Step 5: Check total: 2 + 11 + 6 + 8 + 3 = 30.

Step 6: Histogram bars have heights 2, 11, 6, 8, 3.

Note: In the water-use histogram question, the printed bars add to 150 families, not 110 as stated, and the calculations in the source use 150. Question 1(x) as printed has no single correct option, so it is not used in the MCQs.

Remember

  • Mean, median and mode are measures of central tendency; frequency distribution is not.
  • The value that occurs most often is the mode; data can have 1, 2, 3 or no modes.
  • For even n, median is the mean of the two middle values.
  • Median class is found from cumulative frequency.
  • Always check that frequencies add to the total.

mcqs.q: The arithmetic mean of 1, 0, 5, 5, 6, 7 is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 4. Sum = 1+0+5+5+6+7 = 24 and n = 6, so mean = 24 / 6 = 4.

mcqs.q: The mode of the data 3, 5, 3, 4, 3, 2 is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 3. It occurs three times, more than any other value, so mode = 3.

mcqs.q: The median of the data 2, 3, 4, 5, 10 is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 4. With 5 values in order, the middle (3rd) value is 4, so median = 4.

mcqs.q: The median of the data 0, 2, 4, 2, 6, 8 is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 3. In order 0, 2, 2, 4, 6, 8, median = (2 + 4) / 2 = 3 for even n = 6.

mcqs.q: How many modes are in the data 2, 4, 8, 6, 6, 4, 2?
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 3 modes. Values 2, 4 and 6 each occur twice, so there are three modes in this data.

mcqs.q: The formula for the arithmetic mean is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is X-bar = Σx / n. Mean is the sum of values divided by the number of values.

mcqs.q: The value that occurs more often than other values is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Mode. By definition, the mode is the value that occurs most often in the data.

mcqs.q: If n = 5 and X-bar = 6, then Σx is equal to:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 30. Σx = n x X-bar = 5 x 6 = 30, rearranging the mean formula.

mcqs.q: Presenting raw data in a short and organized manner is called:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is Frequency distribution. It organizes raw data into classes with frequencies in a short form.

mcqs.q: In the water-use histogram (total 150), the median class is:
mcqs.why: The correct answer is 15-20 litres. Cumulative frequencies are 5, 20, 45, 80, so the 75th family falls in the 15-20 class.
